newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Tupras signs 75,000 bpd Iraq oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Tupras signs 75,000 bpd Iraq oil deal.

text.p: Turkey's state-owned refiner Tupras said on Tuesday it had signed a contract with Iraq's state oil marketing organisation SOMO to buy 75,000 bpd of Iraqi oil under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.

Tupras said in a statement that the agreeement would go into effect from today and was equivalent to a value of 3.6 million tonnes of oil a year. Tupras did not give any information on the quality of the oil it would take.
The statement said a Turkish vessel is now en route for the Turkish terminal of Ceyhan to load the oil.

Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said earlier that Iraq had sent two contracts to the U.N. Secretary-General that would enable Iraq to sell the $2 billion worth of oil to international companies.
He said Iraq would give preference to Turkey in selling the oil.
Tupras said the agreement was signed by Tupras general manager Ergun Kuran and his deputy Abdulkadir Basar from the Turkish side.
Tupras has an annual refining capacity of 27.6 million tonnes with refineries in Batman, Izmir, Izmit and Kirikkale.
Iraqi President Saddam Hussein pressed the button that resumed Iraqi oil exports to world markets at 0825 GMT on Tuesday after a six-year break, the official Iraqi News Agency reported.
The United Nations gave Iraq clearance on Monday to start resuming oil exports so that it could buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods.
